cards.name: Blend Mode - Normal
cards.summary: Keyboard command that sets the blend mode of the selected objects back to Normal: the object's colours simply cover what lies below, changed only by its opacity. It removes any Multiply, Screen, Overlay or other mode set earlier.
use_for: resetting a blend mode left on a texture or tint layer after auditioning modes
making a logo or brand colour print exactly as specified, without mixing with the background
cleaning up artwork before PDF/X-1a or flattened print export, where blend modes force transparency flattening
avoid: when the object is also faded: Normal keeps the opacity, use Opacity - 100% as well
to strip every appearance attribute (effects, extra fills): use the Appearance panel instead
expecting the shortcut to work out of the box: it has none until you assign one
cards.how: Select the objects (or target a group or layer), then press the shortcut you assigned. It has no default key: add one in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts, Tools set, where the blend-mode and opacity commands sit together. It sets the same value as picking Normal in the Transparency panel's mode menu.
cards.script_api: No invoke was harvested: the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Blend Mode Normal", and it is a keyboard command, not a tool, so selectTool is not expected to run it. Same result through the DOM: for each item of app.activeDocument.selection set item.blendingMode = BlendModes.NORMAL (PageItem.blendingMode; works on paths, groups, text frames and placed images).

review.changes: how: dropped the Isolate Blending sentence copied from the blend-mode template (Normal has no blend to isolate); rest checked: BlendModes.NORMAL / PageItem.blendingMode in the ai_api harvest, PS Normal and CDR Toolbox/Transparency (cdrMergeNormal) exist

cards.name: Blend Mode - Overlay
cards.summary: Keyboard command that sets the selected objects to the Overlay blend mode: the object multiplies over dark areas and screens over light areas of what is below, so contrast rises and the base keeps its highlights and shadows while taking on the object's colour or texture.
use_for: laying a grain, paper or halftone texture over a flat vector illustration
tinting a placed photo with a brand colour while keeping its shading
adding punchy light-and-shadow gradients over a poster background
avoid: over pure white or pure black areas: they stay white or black, so nothing shows; try Multiply or Screen
for a gentle effect: Overlay is strong, Soft Light is the softer version
where exact print colour matters: the result is computed in the document colour mode (RGB and CMYK files look different) and is flattened on PDF/X-1a export
cards.how: Select the objects (or target a group or layer), then press the shortcut you assigned. It has no default key: add one in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts, Tools set, where the blend-mode and opacity commands sit together. It sets the same value as picking Overlay in the Transparency panel's mode menu; Isolate Blending there limits the blend to the objects inside a group.
cards.script_api: No invoke was harvested: the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Blend Mode Overlay", and it is a keyboard command, not a tool, so selectTool is not expected to run it. Same result through the DOM: for each item of app.activeDocument.selection set item.blendingMode = BlendModes.OVERLAY (PageItem.blendingMode; works on paths, groups, text frames and placed images).

review.changes: none: BlendModes value and PageItem.blendingMode in the ai_api harvest, the spot-colour / white-black behaviour matches Illustrator's documented blend rules, PS blend mode and CDR Toolbox/Transparency (cdrMergeMode has the mode) exist

cards.name: Blend Mode - Previous Mode
cards.summary: Keyboard command that, judging by its name and its place after Blend Mode - Next Mode in the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog, steps the selected objects' blend mode one entry back in the Transparency panel's mode list (for example from Screen to Lighten). Whether it wraps around at Normal, and what it does when the selection has mixed modes, is not confirmed: the harvest probe never reached this id.
use_for: auditioning blend modes on a texture or colour overlay without opening the Transparency panel
quickly comparing Multiply against Color Burn on a shadow shape in an illustration
flipping through looks for a duotone or tint layer on a placed photo
avoid: when you already know the mode: use the direct command (Blend Mode - Overlay, Screen ...) or the Transparency panel
on a selection whose objects carry different modes: the result is not confirmed, select one look-alike set at a time
expecting a default key: none is assigned
cards.how: Select the objects, then press the shortcut you assigned (there is none by default; set it in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts, Tools set, ideally next to Next Mode). Each press moves one mode up the list Normal / Darken, Multiply, Color Burn / Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge / Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light / Difference, Exclusion / Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity, so you can watch the artwork change mode by mode.

Same result through the DOM: read item.blendingMode, find it in [BlendModes.NORMAL, BlendModes.DARKEN, BlendModes.MULTIPLY, BlendModes.COLORBURN, BlendModes.LIGHTEN, BlendModes.SCREEN, BlendModes.COLORDODGE, BlendModes.OVERLAY, BlendModes.SOFTLIGHT, BlendModes.HARDLIGHT, BlendModes.DIFFERENCE, BlendModes.EXCLUSION, BlendModes.HUE, BlendModes.SATURATIONBLEND, BlendModes.COLORBLEND, BlendModes.LUMINOSITY] (the Transparency panel order in the ai_blend_mode harvest) and assign the previous one.

cards.name: Blend Mode - Saturation

use_for: turning the part of a placed photo under a grey shape black-and-white (colour-splash look)
muting a busy background behind a headline with a low-saturation shape
boosting colour intensity in one area of an illustration with a saturated shape
avoid: with spot colours: Illustrator does not blend spot colours in Saturation (or Hue, Color, Luminosity, Difference, Exclusion) mode
to desaturate whole artwork for good: Edit > Edit Colors > Convert to Grayscale changes the colours themselves
over neutral grey or black-and-white areas: there is no saturation to keep or change, so nothing happens

It sets the same value as picking Saturation in the Transparency panel's mode menu; Isolate Blending there limits the blend to the objects inside a group.

cards.name: Blend Mode - Screen

glows, light rays and neon highlights on a dark poster
lightening a photo area under a coloured shape for a faded, airy look
avoid: on a white or very light background: there is nothing left to lighten, so the object vanishes
to darken or add shadows: use Multiply
when the image needs a clean cut-out edge rather than a lightened blend: mask or clip it instead

cards.name: Blend Mode - Soft Light
cards.summary: Keyboard command that sets the selected objects to the Soft Light blend mode: where the object is lighter than 50% grey it gently lightens what is below (like dodging), where darker it gently darkens (like burning). It is the subtle sibling of Overlay and Hard Light.
use_for: soft shading and highlight shapes on flat character or icon illustrations
a gentle colour cast over a placed photo for a warm or cool mood
a subtle paper or noise texture that should not overpower the artwork
avoid: when the effect must be strong or high-contrast: use Overlay or Hard Light
with a mid-grey object: 50% grey leaves the base unchanged
for exact print colour: the blend is computed in the document colour mode and flattened on PDF/X-1a export
cards.how: Select the objects (or target a group or layer), then press the shortcut you assigned. It has no default key: add one in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts, Tools set, where the blend-mode and opacity commands sit together. It sets the same value as picking Soft Light in the Transparency panel's mode menu; Isolate Blending there limits the blend to the objects inside a group.

cards.name: Color
cards.summary: Keyboard command (the Color button under the Fill and Stroke boxes in the toolbar) that sets the active box, Fill or Stroke, back to the last solid colour used. On selected objects the fill or stroke turns that colour, replacing a gradient, pattern or None.
use_for: bringing a fill back after setting it to None while building an icon
replacing a gradient fill with flat colour on a shape for a flat-design version
putting a solid stroke back on an outline that was set to None
avoid: while editing text: it types a comma; press Esc first
to pick a particular colour: click a swatch or use the Color panel / eyedropper
when the wrong attribute changes: press X so the box you want is in front first
cards.how: Choose the target box first (X toggles Fill / Stroke; the front box is active), select the objects, then press the comma key or click the Color button. The Color panel shows the colour so you can change it right away. Do it with no text cursor active, otherwise a comma is typed.
cards.script_api: No invoke was harvested: the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Paint Color", and it is a keyboard command, not a tool, so selectTool is not expected to run it. A script cannot read Illustrator's last-used colour, but it can set any solid colour: check app.isFillActive() / app.isStrokeActive(), then set PathItem.fillColor (with filled = true) or strokeColor (with stroked = true) to an RGBColor / CMYKColor / SpotColor; Document.defaultFillColor and defaultStrokeColor do the same for new objects.

review.changes: none: ',' matches the batch; isFillActive / isStrokeActive, fillColor / strokeColor, defaultFillColor / defaultStrokeColor in the harvest; X (Toggle Fill/Stroke) harvested

cards.name: Decrease Diameter
cards.summary: Keyboard command that makes the brush of the current brush-type tool smaller, one step per press: the Blob Brush, the Eraser and the Symbolism tools (diameter of the spray area). The size circle around the cursor shrinks to show the new diameter.
use_for: fine detail work with the Blob Brush on an inked illustration or lettering
a small eraser for cleaning up line art edges
tightening the Symbolism spray area when adding small details to a pattern
avoid: confusing it with Ctrl+[ (Object > Arrange > Send Backward)
while editing text: it types a bracket
to change the weight of Paintbrush or Pencil strokes: set the Stroke weight or the brush options instead
cards.how: With the Blob Brush, Eraser or a Symbolism tool active, press [ to shrink the brush and ] (Increase Diameter) to grow it, between strokes. For an exact size, double-click the tool and type the Size / Diameter in its options. Symbolism intensity is a separate command, Symbolism Tools - Decrease Intensity (Shift+{ in the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog).
cards.script_api: No invoke was harvested: the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Tool Dec Diameter", and it is a keyboard command, not a tool, so selectTool is not expected to run it. Tool diameters are not exposed in the scripting DOM and Blob Brush / Eraser strokes cannot be replayed. A script builds the shapes directly instead (pathItems.ellipse / rectangle / setEntirePath) and merges them: group with app.executeMenuCommand("group") (Effect > Pathfinder needs a group), then app.executeMenuCommand("Live Pathfinder Add") and app.executeMenuCommand("expandStyle").

review.changes: how: the intensity command's harvested shortcut is Shift+{ (card said Shift+[), now named with its harvested name; script_api: the Pathfinder merge now groups first and names the harvested ids (group, Live Pathfinder Add, expandStyle)

cards.name: Default
cards.summary: Keyboard command (the Default Fill and Stroke button in the toolbar) that resets fill and stroke to the defaults, white fill and black stroke, for the selected objects and for objects drawn next. It may also drop extra appearance attributes such as added fills, brushes or effects; check the Appearance panel.
use_for: resetting a shape with a messy or unknown appearance before restyling it
starting a wireframe or layout sketch with plain outlined boxes
getting back to a visible stroke and fill after drawing with None set
avoid: on objects whose effects or brush strokes you want to keep: they may be removed; edit fill and stroke in the Appearance panel instead
while editing text: it types the letter d; press Esc first
when only the colours should swap: use Swap Fill/Stroke (Shift+X)
cards.how: Select the objects and press D (with no text cursor active) or click the small default icon next to the Fill and Stroke boxes. With nothing selected it only resets the boxes, so the next shape is drawn white with a black stroke.
cards.script_api: No invoke was harvested: the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Default Fill Stroke", and it is a keyboard command, not a tool, so selectTool is not expected to run it. Same colours through the DOM: on each selected PathItem set filled = true, fillColor = a white RGBColor / CMYKColor, stroked = true, strokeColor = black, strokeWidth = 1 (the usual default weight; the harvest does not record what D sets); Document.defaultFilled / defaultFillColor / defaultStroked / defaultStrokeColor / defaultStrokeWidth do it for new objects. Removing effects or brushes has no direct DOM call.

review.changes: summary: dropped the 1 pt stroke weight (in neither the batch nor the harvest; script_api keeps 1 flagged as the usual value); avoid: pressing D in text types a lower-case d, not D

cards.name: Gradient
cards.summary: Keyboard command (the Gradient button under the Fill and Stroke boxes) that applies the last-used gradient, a white-to-black linear gradient if none has been used yet, to the active Fill or Stroke of the selected objects, ready for editing in the Gradient panel.
use_for: starting a background gradient on a poster or social post rectangle
giving a logo shape or button a quick light-to-dark gradient to refine
applying a gradient to a stroke for gradient outlines or lettering
avoid: while editing text: it types a period; press Esc first
for many-point painterly colour: use a Freeform gradient in the Gradient panel or a gradient mesh
when you need one specific saved gradient: click its swatch instead of relying on the last-used one
cards.how: Pick the target box (X toggles Fill / Stroke), select the objects and press the period key or click the Gradient button. Then edit stops, angle and type in the Gradient panel or drag with the Gradient Tool (G) on the artwork (fill gradients only; a stroke gradient is edited in the Gradient panel). Do it with no text cursor active.
cards.script_api: No invoke was harvested: the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Paint Gradient", and it is a keyboard command, not a tool, so selectTool is not expected to run it. A script cannot read the last-used gradient, but it applies any gradient: make a GradientColor, set its gradient to an item of app.activeDocument.gradients (or a new one with gradientStops), then set PathItem.fillColor or strokeColor to it.
